reasoning: The claim overstates and mischaracterizes the findings of a widely cited March 2023 Goldman Sachs report. The report estimated that generative AI could expose the equivalent of approximately 300 million full-time jobs to automation globally, rather than definitively predicting that 300 million workers will be laid off or replaced. Crucially, the authors distinguished between tasks being automated and entire jobs being eliminated, noting that most occupations would be complemented rather than substituted by AI. Additionally, the study noted that technological disruption historically drives new job creation and estimated a significant boost to global GDP over time. Framing this projection as a definitive forecast that AI "will replace 300 million jobs" ignores these essential economic nuances.
